target_customer: AI labs and companies that need training and evaluation environments for agents
problem: Agents lack realistic environments to learn the tacit knowledge needed to run a business. ORO builds simulations grounded in real data.
business_model: Benchmarks and RL environments, likely sold to AI labs (not stated)

founders.name: Seth Schilbe
prior_employers: AWS (senior software engineer, ECS and Cloud Map)
education: University of New Brunswick, Software Engineering degree

competitors.name: YC-Bench and similar simulated business benchmarks
competitors.what: Benchmarks for long-horizon agents in simulated companies

competitors.name: Bespoke Labs
competitors.what: Simulated worlds and RL environments for agents

competitors.name: Mechanize, Fleet AI, HUD, Veris AI, Plato
competitors.what: Environment-native startups, roughly 20 seed to Series A in 2026

technical_complexity.rationale: High-fidelity simulations that transfer to real business outcomes are research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Environments can be copied, and labs often build their own. Grounding in real data could help but is unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Many funded vendors and in-house efforts target RL environments.

market_need_then: 2025 and 2026 coverage describes labs paying for RL environments as a scarce input to agent training.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand evidence. The name collides with ORO Labs, a procurement software company, and with Oro the Bittensor-related ORO benchmark.

outcome_analysis: ORO AI is a Fall 2026 YC company with no exit or reported round. Strengths are founders with distributed systems and Bittensor-ecosystem experience, and backers listed on the site include Crucible Labs, which employed one founder. The risk is a crowded environment market and no visible revenue.
notes: Backers listed on its site: Y Combinator, Crucible Labs, Unsupervised Capital, Savant, with no amounts, so no rounds recorded. A search summary described the product as a shopping-agent benchmark (ORO Bench, a Bittensor subnet), which conflicts with the YC description of SMB Bench; unresolved. A $6M seed for an unrelated ORO AI and ORO Labs rounds are different companies.
